summary: 1941 Forest Service fire tower on Glassy Mountain, Rabun County, GA; standing, sometimes staffed, reached by a locked gate and a hike.

facts.design: 55-foot metal tower with a 13x13-foot CL-100 series live-in cab and catwalk (register); the Weebly listing calls it a 55-foot steel K-brace replacement tower

staffing.status: sometimes staffed; many visitors report it unstaffed

access.note: Dirt road ends at a locked vehicle barrier gate about 1 mile from the tower. The sources state no climbing rule.

visit.trail_note: From the locked gate about a mile from the tower, the rest of the way is a climb up the mountain

events.note: Ground residence and garage added in the 1960s; sources give the decade only, so 1960 is a placeholder
Registered July 26, 2007; nominated by John Mayer
Visit report dated September 2, 2018: good condition overall; rust on the cab; windows broken; staffing listed as sometimes

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and Wikipedia both say built 1941. Weebly calls the current 55-foot tower a replacement, with no date or reason. Recorded 1941 as the build date; the replacement is left unexplained.
Register lists staffing as sometimes and says many visitors found it unstaffed. Recorded as sometimes staffed rather than either extreme.

notes_for_editor: Replacement question is open: Weebly says the current tower is a replacement, but NHLR and Wikipedia date the tower to 1941 with no replacement mentioned. Access 'restricted' is my reading of the locked gate; no climbing rule in the sources. The 1960s event is coded as 1960 (decade only). The register gives 3,315 ft elevation, matching the brief's 1010.4 m; the tnlandforms list gives 3449 ft and was not used. Register coordinates match the brief. No new photos added.
